title: Tutorial 03 - Foreign Land Ownership Restrictions and Unlimited Companies
description: Exam-standard MCQs based on the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014 and Unlimited Companies.
subject: LAW2372 - Corporate Law

questions.question: Emerald Holdings (Pvt) Ltd is incorporated in Sri Lanka. Forty-eight percent of its shares are held directly by foreign investors while another six percent is held by a Sri Lankan company wholly owned by foreign nationals. Emerald proposes to purchase freehold land in Galle. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The purchase is permitted because direct foreign ownership remains below fifty percent.
The purchase is prohibited because both direct and indirect foreign ownership must be considered.
The purchase is valid provided the company has traded in Sri Lanka for more than ten years.
The purchase is valid because only overseas companies are restricted from acquiring land.
questions.answer: The purchase is prohibited because both direct and indirect foreign ownership must be considered.
questions.rationale: The Act aggregates direct and indirect foreign ownership when applying the fifty percent threshold.

questions.question: Blue Ocean Ltd is a Sri Lankan company with forty-five percent foreign shareholding when it acquires freehold land. Twelve years later foreign ownership increases to fifty-two percent and remains unchanged. Which consequence best reflects the Act?
options: The acquisition remains permanently valid because the threshold was satisfied on the date of transfer.
The company breaches the statutory requirement to maintain foreign ownership below fifty percent for twenty consecutive years.
The company immediately becomes an overseas company.
The transfer automatically converts into a ninety-nine-year lease.
questions.answer: The company breaches the statutory requirement to maintain foreign ownership below fifty percent for twenty consecutive years.
questions.rationale: The below-fifty-percent level must continue for twenty consecutive years after transfer.

questions.question: A listed Sri Lankan company exceeds the statutory foreign shareholding threshold after an international share issue. Which period is generally available to restore compliance?
options: Six months from the date of exceeding the threshold.
Twelve months from the date of exceeding the threshold.
Twenty-four months from the date of the annual general meeting.
Until the next audited financial statements are filed.
questions.answer: Twelve months from the date of exceeding the threshold.
questions.rationale: Quoted companies receive twelve months whereas other companies receive six months.

questions.question: A foreign corporation leases commercial land in Sri Lanka for one hundred and twenty years. Both parties execute the deed and pay every applicable tax. Which legal position is strongest?
options: The lease is fully enforceable because taxes have been paid.
The lease is valid only for the first ninety-nine years.
The lease becomes void only if the Registrar refuses registration.
The lease automatically converts into freehold ownership after ninety-nine years.
questions.answer: The lease is valid only for the first ninety-nine years.
questions.rationale: The Act limits foreign leases to ninety-nine years; any excess is ineffective.

questions.question: A foreign-owned company operating continuously in Sri Lanka for eleven years enters into a sixty-year commercial lease outside any BOI zone. Which Land Lease Tax rate most likely applies?
options: Zero percent because the company has operated for more than ten years.
Seven point five percent because it satisfies a statutory qualifying condition.
Fifteen percent because only BOI land qualifies for any reduction.
Fifteen percent because the reduced rate applies only to condominium units.
questions.answer: Seven point five percent because it satisfies a statutory qualifying condition.
questions.rationale: Ten or more consecutive years of active operation qualifies for the reduced rate.

questions.question: A foreign investor leases an apartment located on the fifth floor of a condominium for thirty years. Which statement best reflects the applicable Land Lease Tax position?
options: The lease qualifies for the reduced seven point five percent rate.
The lease is entirely exempt from Land Lease Tax.
The lease attracts the standard rate because only freehold purchases benefit.
The lease is prohibited because foreigners cannot lease condominiums.
questions.answer: The lease qualifies for the reduced seven point five percent rate.
questions.rationale: Qualifying fourth-floor-and-above condominiums with leases below thirty-five years receive the reduced rate.

questions.question: A foreign company wishes to purchase a condominium unit situated on the third floor. Full consideration has already been remitted into Sri Lanka before transfer. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: The purchase is permitted because payment was made through inward remittance.
The purchase remains prohibited because the statutory floor requirement is not satisfied.
The purchase becomes valid after Cabinet approval alone.
The purchase is automatically converted into a lease.
questions.answer: The purchase remains prohibited because the statutory floor requirement is not satisfied.
questions.rationale: The exemption applies only to qualifying units on or above the fourth floor.

questions.question: Which individual is primarily responsible for certifying every six months that foreign shareholding has remained below the statutory threshold during the twenty-year monitoring period?
options: Chairman of the Board
Registrar of Companies
Company Secretary
External Auditor
questions.answer: Company Secretary
questions.rationale: The Company Secretary has the continuing reporting obligation.

questions.question: Which authority is principally responsible for collecting Land Lease Tax imposed under the Act?
options: Registrar of Lands
Commissioner General of Inland Revenue
Registrar of Companies
Surveyor General
questions.answer: Commissioner General of Inland Revenue
questions.rationale: The Commissioner General administers Land Lease Tax collection.

questions.question: A foreign-owned company validly acquires land under one of the statutory exemptions. Two years later it offers the land as security to a licensed commercial bank. Which statement is legally strongest?
options: The mortgage is unrestricted because ownership was lawfully acquired.
The mortgage is prohibited during the first five years following the transfer.
Only foreign banks may accept the mortgage during the first five years.
The restriction applies only to leases and not to ownership.
questions.answer: The mortgage is prohibited during the first five years following the transfer.
questions.rationale: The Act imposes a five-year prohibition on mortgaging qualifying land.

questions.question: Lion Corporate Services recommends incorporating as an Unlimited Liability Company solely to avoid the foreign ownership restrictions contained in the Land Act. Which advice is legally correct?
options: The recommendation is correct because unlimited companies are exempt from the Act.
The recommendation is incorrect because the decisive test is foreign shareholding rather than company type.
The recommendation is correct only where the company owns subsidiaries.
The recommendation is correct if the company does not issue ordinary shares.
questions.answer: The recommendation is incorrect because the decisive test is foreign shareholding rather than company type.
questions.rationale: The Land Act applies irrespective of whether the company is limited or unlimited.

questions.question: A Sri Lankan Unlimited Liability Company has one hundred percent Sri Lankan ownership and intends to purchase agricultural land. Which statement best reflects the legal position?
options: The purchase is prohibited because unlimited companies cannot own land.
The purchase is generally permissible because there is no disqualifying foreign ownership.
The purchase requires Cabinet approval solely because the company is unlimited.
The purchase is valid only if the company converts into a private limited company.
questions.answer: The purchase is generally permissible because there is no disqualifying foreign ownership.
questions.rationale: Unlimited companies are not restricted merely because of their liability structure.

questions.question: Which commercial advantage most commonly explains why sophisticated corporate groups intentionally choose an Unlimited Liability Company?
options: Automatic exemption from corporate taxation.
Greater access to public equity markets.
Reduced public disclosure of financial information.
Freedom from directors' fiduciary duties.
questions.answer: Reduced public disclosure of financial information.
questions.rationale: Commercial privacy is one of the principal reasons for using ULCs.

questions.question: A multinational group proposes using an Unlimited Liability Company as a wholly owned holding company. Which explanation best justifies this decision?
options: Unlimited liability eliminates every regulatory obligation imposed on holding companies.
The parent already bears the economic risk while obtaining additional financial privacy.
Unlimited companies cannot become subsidiaries.
Holding companies are legally required to adopt the unlimited company structure.
questions.answer: The parent already bears the economic risk while obtaining additional financial privacy.
questions.rationale: This is the principal commercial justification discussed in practice.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes member liability in an Unlimited Liability Company during winding up?
options: Members contribute only up to the unpaid amount on their shares.
Members contribute only after every creditor has waived recovery.
Members may be personally required to satisfy company debts if company assets are insufficient.
Members incur liability only where fraud is established.
questions.answer: Members may be personally required to satisfy company debts if company assets are insufficient.
questions.rationale: Unlimited liability removes the statutory cap on members' liability upon winding up.

questions.question: Aurora Holdings (Pvt) Ltd is 48% foreign-owned when it acquires freehold land. Two years later, a restructuring causes foreign ownership to increase to 51%. Four months after the increase, the company reduces foreign ownership back to 49%. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The company has complied because foreign ownership was restored below 50% before six months elapsed.
The company permanently loses ownership because the threshold can never be exceeded.
The company remains compliant because the 20-year rule only applies to public companies.
The company automatically converts into an offshore company.
questions.answer: The company has complied because foreign ownership was restored below 50% before six months elapsed.
questions.rationale: Non-quoted companies have six months to restore compliance after exceeding the threshold.

questions.question: A foreign corporation leases land for 95 years inside a BOI-approved industrial zone. Which statement best reflects the legal consequences?
options: The lease is prohibited because foreign companies cannot lease land.
The lease is valid and generally qualifies for the reduced 7.5% Land Lease Tax.
The lease is exempt from both Stamp Duty and Land Lease Tax.
The lease automatically becomes freehold ownership after registration.
questions.answer: The lease is valid and generally qualifies for the reduced 7.5% Land Lease Tax.
questions.rationale: Land situated within qualifying BOI zones is one of the statutory grounds for the reduced rate.

questions.question: A company secretary fails to submit the required six-month compliance reports for three consecutive reporting periods, although foreign ownership remained below 50% throughout. Which statement is legally strongest?
options: No breach exists because the company satisfied the ownership requirement.
The reporting obligation is independent of the ownership requirement, creating an ongoing compliance failure.
Only the Registrar of Companies may require such reports.
The reports become unnecessary once the first five years have passed.
questions.answer: The reporting obligation is independent of the ownership requirement, creating an ongoing compliance failure.
questions.rationale: The Company Secretary has an ongoing statutory reporting obligation throughout the monitoring period.

questions.question: A foreign individual inherits freehold land in Sri Lanka from a Sri Lankan parent through intestate succession. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The inheritance is prohibited because foreigners can never acquire freehold land.
The transfer falls within a statutory exemption relating to succession.
The beneficiary must immediately sell the property within six months.
Ownership is allowed only after Cabinet approval.
questions.answer: The transfer falls within a statutory exemption relating to succession.
questions.rationale: Inheritance by intestacy, gift or will to qualifying foreign next of kin is specifically exempted.

questions.question: A foreign company purchases a condominium unit located on the fifth floor. Full consideration was remitted into Sri Lanka after the transfer deed was executed. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The exemption is unavailable because the inward foreign remittance requirement was not satisfied before transfer.
The exemption applies because the property is above the fourth floor.
Timing of payment is legally irrelevant once foreign funds are remitted.
Foreign companies cannot purchase condominium units under any circumstances.
questions.answer: The exemption is unavailable because the inward foreign remittance requirement was not satisfied before transfer.
questions.rationale: The exemption requires the full purchase price to be remitted before the transfer.

questions.question: A foreign-owned company has operated in Sri Lanka for nine years and eleven months when it enters into a lease agreement. Which Land Lease Tax rate most likely applies?
options: 7.5% because the company has substantially satisfied the operational requirement.
15% because the statutory ten-year requirement has not yet been met.
0% because the company is already established in Sri Lanka.
7.5% because all companies with more than 50% foreign ownership qualify.
questions.answer: 15% because the statutory ten-year requirement has not yet been met.
questions.rationale: The reduced rate requires at least ten consecutive years of operation.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly demonstrates indirect foreign ownership exceeding the statutory threshold?
options: A Sri Lankan company owns 55% of another Sri Lankan company while itself being wholly Sri Lankan-owned.
A foreign parent owns 60% of Company A, which owns 60% of Company B.
Two Sri Lankan citizens jointly own 60% of the shares.
Foreign lenders provide 70% of the company's borrowings.
questions.answer: A foreign parent owns 60% of Company A, which owns 60% of Company B.
questions.rationale: Indirect ownership through a chain of companies is expressly considered under the Act.

questions.question: Which authority possesses the primary responsibility for determining whether a transfer or lease should be registered under the Act?
options: Commissioner General of Inland Revenue.
Registrar of Lands.
Registrar of Companies.
Secretary to the Treasury.
questions.answer: Registrar of Lands.
questions.rationale: The Registrar of Lands registers deeds and may reject non-compliant transactions.

questions.question: A Sri Lankan Unlimited Liability Company has 55% foreign shareholding but argues that unlimited member liability provides sufficient creditor protection to justify owning land. Which statement is legally strongest?
options: The argument succeeds because unlimited liability removes the statutory restriction.
The argument fails because liability structure is irrelevant under the Land Act.
The argument succeeds if all creditors consent.
The argument succeeds only where the company has operated for ten years.
questions.answer: The argument fails because liability structure is irrelevant under the Land Act.
questions.rationale: The decisive criterion is foreign shareholding, not the type of company.

questions.question: A Sri Lankan company owns land while maintaining 49% foreign shareholding. During the twentieth year after acquisition, foreign ownership increases to 52%. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The statutory maintenance period has not yet been fully completed, creating a compliance issue.
The company automatically satisfies the Act because nineteen years is substantially equivalent to twenty.
The increase is irrelevant after the first ten years.
The company immediately becomes exempt as a mature business.
questions.answer: The statutory maintenance period has not yet been fully completed, creating a compliance issue.
questions.rationale: The below-50% threshold must be maintained for twenty consecutive years.

questions.question: A company chooses the Unlimited Liability Company structure primarily because it wishes to avoid publishing detailed financial information. Which feature most directly supports this objective?
options: Unlimited companies generally enjoy reduced public disclosure of annual accounts.
Unlimited companies are exempt from accounting standards.
Unlimited companies cannot be audited.
Unlimited companies are exempt from maintaining accounting records.
questions.answer: Unlimited companies generally enjoy reduced public disclosure of annual accounts.
questions.rationale: Commercial privacy is one of the principal reasons sophisticated businesses adopt ULCs.

questions.question: A foreign investor wishes to sublease state land previously leased from the Government. Which additional legal requirement applies?
options: Prior written approval of the relevant Minister.
Approval from the Commissioner General of Inland Revenue.
Approval from every shareholder of the lessee company.
No additional approval is required.
questions.answer: Prior written approval of the relevant Minister.
questions.rationale: State land cannot be sub-let or sub-leased without ministerial approval.

questions.question: Which situation best illustrates why an Unlimited Liability Company is commonly used as an intra-group holding company?
options: The parent company already effectively bears the financial risk while obtaining additional commercial privacy.
Unlimited liability completely eliminates taxation on dividends.
Unlimited companies are exempt from corporate governance rules.
Unlimited companies may publicly issue shares without restriction.
questions.answer: The parent company already effectively bears the financial risk while obtaining additional commercial privacy.
questions.rationale: The risk already exists within the corporate group, making privacy the principal commercial advantage.

questions.question: Which of the following transactions is LEAST likely to qualify for any statutory concession under the tutorial?
options: A lease within a declared BOI industrial estate.
Purchase of a fifth-floor condominium using full inward remittance before transfer.
A foreign-owned company operating in Sri Lanka for eleven consecutive years leasing commercial land.
Purchase of ordinary commercial land by a newly incorporated foreign company.
questions.answer: Purchase of ordinary commercial land by a newly incorporated foreign company.
questions.rationale: None of the statutory exemptions or qualifying concessions apply.

questions.question: Which combination of facts would most strongly support a conclusion that a foreign-owned company may lease land while benefiting from the reduced Land Lease Tax rate?
options: Foreign-owned company, eight years of operation, lease outside qualifying areas.
Foreign-owned company, eleven years of active operation, sixty-year lease.
Foreign-owned company, newly incorporated, ninety-nine-year lease.
Foreign-owned company, six years of operation, ordinary commercial lease.
questions.answer: Foreign-owned company, eleven years of active operation, sixty-year lease.
questions.rationale: More than ten consecutive years of active operation satisfies one of the principal statutory grounds for the reduced 7.5% Land Lease Tax rate.
